land_owner.value: The ground was entered by Robert A Kenzie, 7 May 1831
land_owner.note: KINZIE'S ADDITION. The north fraction of section 10 is the section north of the river, which is why the register prints 102.29 acres and not a quarter's 160. It is resolved as the section's own grid box clipped to the committed north bank of the main stem (`e1834_harbor_cut/shoreline.geojson`), so no boundary here is authored. The two rows the register carries for it — one plain, one with the school-section marker — are the same entry printed twice. THE REGISTER SPELLS THE PURCHASER MORE THAN ONE WAY for this same tract — Robert A Kenzie; Robert A Kinzie — and the spellings are carried rather than merged, which is the land_sales crosswalk's standing rule: tract agreement is where two spellings MIGHT be one man and is never proof that they are. THE ROOF IS AN INVENTION AND THIS CANNOT OUTRANK IT. The footprint stands 81 m inside the tract's nearest boundary, which on a documented building would carry the middle tier, but this building was dealt to its lot by a recipe and is not there. The tract is real and the register's words about it are read; what is graded here is the claim that THIS roof stands on it, and that claim is the recipe's. WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It claims that the tract the Illinois State Archives' land-sale register describes contains this structure's committed position — the patent for this ground was ENTERED by this man on this date. It does not claim he still held the ground on 1 July 1835, that he lived here, or that he ever stood on it: a sale is a transaction, and the register's only column about residence names a county. THE SECTION LINES ARE CONSTRUCTED, NOT TRACED (L219): the grid is carried from the single PLSS corner at State & Madison, on the plat's own east-west bearing, in nominal one-mile squares.

persons.name: William Allen
persons.note: GRADED BY THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER — rule G2e, applied 2026-09-04. This identity is inferred because that rung fired on the civic and press rows recorded on this card, which the resident-research corpus does not read. This programme's letter-list rule of 2026-09-02 would call it a projected resident on the absence of a research row; it is superseded here, and a no-find in one corpus is not a finding about another (T-0822). KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Allen, William' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1). THE 1840 FEDERAL CENSUS — A HEAD FIVE YEARS AFTER THE SCENE, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1840 federal census of Chicago, read line by line off the left sheets in this repository, carries 1 head of this name — “Wm. Allen” (33S7-9YYJ-NY, printed page 230, line 26). This project has ruled the head a MATCH for this person: the full name agrees, it is unique on both sides, and a discriminator independent of the name — directory persistence — separately places the same person in Chicago after the 1840 book was taken. Under the rule that decided it (L6 matched), by the crosswalk's own ladder (data/research/census_1840/resident_crosswalk.json). LATER EVIDENCE ONLY. The ratified grading ladder binds: an 1839 or 1840 appearance alone is never an 1835 resident, and 1840 household composition is never back-projected to the 1835-07-01 scene. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and an 1840 head is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Allen, Willard | Profession. | September 15, 1876.” (second_presb_0002, printed page 154), admitted 1876-09-15 by profession. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Allen' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins W. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

persons.name: Willard Jones
persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST AND A SECOND INDEPENDENT SOURCE. Read from poll_1834, poll_1835, tax_1833. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. PRESENT AT CHICAGO ON 19 OCTOBER 1833, FROM THE CATALOGUE OF THE FOURTEEN BAPTISTS WHO ORGANISED THE FIRST BAPTIST SOCIETY. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois, vol. 2 (1895), printed page 294 (claim bk_mose2_010; data/research/books/claims/moses_kirkland_history_of_chicago_v2.json): "At the date of the organization of the First Baptist society, October 19, 1833, there were twenty-five Baptists in the settlement, fourteen of whom were present and connected themselves with the new enterprise. The catalogue of those present is: Rev. Allen B. Freeman and Hannah C., his wife, S. T. Jackson, Martin D. Harmon, Peter Moore, Nathaniel Carpenter, John K. Sargent, Peter Warden, Willard Jones, Ebenezer and Betsey Crane, Susanna Rice, Samantha Harmon and Lucinda Jackson." THE CATALOGUE NAMES 'Willard Jones' and the crosswalk joined it to this card on the forename alone, which is the whole join and is enough: this project holds six Joneses and 'Willard' reaches exactly one. A PRESENCE IS NOT AN ARRIVAL, AND IT BOUNDS ONE: a person standing in the settlement on 19 October 1833 had reached it by that day, so the bound is carried at 1833-10-19 with `not_later_than` precision — the same kind of statement the register made, moved earlier by a reading that saw the person sooner. THE CATALOGUE IS A ROLL AND NOT A CENSUS: the compiler says twenty-five Baptists were in the settlement and names the fourteen who were PRESENT that day, so the list is a floor. It can date the people it names and it can never be read to exclude anybody it leaves out. THE GRADE CEILING IS THE SOURCE'S AND NOT THIS FIELD'S. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois (1895) is a compiler sixty years after the fact, crediting Andreas and Hurlbut on the pages read here; every claim taken off it is transcription_mediated and none is scan_verified, so nothing drawn from it is graded above `inferred` however plainly it is printed (the rule T-1322 set for the settlers table, kept here). AND IT ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION THAN PRESENCE ON THE SCENE DATE: being in the settlement in October 1833 says nothing about 1 July 1835, so `present_on_scene_date` is untouched and goes on reading `uncertain`. THE REGISTER'S BOUND IS NOT LOST, IT IS SUBSUMED: a person present in October 1833 was necessarily in the town when the record below first named them. PRIOR NOTE, KEPT: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. tax_1833 stands against this person's name by 31 December 1833 and nothing says when they came. THE 1833 TAX LIST IS A PROPERTY ROLL, NOT A RESIDENCE CHECK (T-1117): it names the owner of ground inside the town, resident or not, and its own entry 110 is a man three years dead. It bounds the town's RECORD of this name and not the day this person reached Chicago. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the town's own paper carries this name by 1 July 1835; whether the man it names was standing in the town is a claim this record cannot make, and present_on_scene_date says `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 3 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Jones, Willard” (tax_1833_053, line 105); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Jones, Willard” (poll_1834_061, line 230); Poll list of 1835 — “Jones, Willard” (poll_1835_037, line 324). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Jones' agrees with the entry's forenames; 5 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 3 times, as “JONES WILLARD”, 1833-10-22 to 1833-10-25: 3 parcels of the school section — lot 3 of block 96 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 5 of block 118 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 6 of block 96 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $308.00 (ls0258, ls0259, ls0260). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: JONES WILLARD matches Willard Jones: the forename names Willard Jones of the 6 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

persons.name: Ira Kimberly
persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST AND A SECOND INDEPENDENT SOURCE. Read from poll_1835, tax_1833. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. tax_1833 stands against this person's name by 31 December 1833 and nothing says when they came. THE 1833 TAX LIST IS A PROPERTY ROLL, NOT A RESIDENCE CHECK (T-1117): it names the owner of ground inside the town, resident or not, and its own entry 110 is a man three years dead. It bounds the town's RECORD of this name and not the day this person reached Chicago. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the town's own paper carries this name by 1 July 1835; whether the man it names was standing in the town is a claim this record cannot make, and present_on_scene_date says `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Kimberly, Ira” (tax_1833_058, line 110); Poll list of 1835 — “Kimberly, Ira” (poll_1835_040, line 327). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Kimberly' agrees with the entry's forenames; 3 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

persons.name: Alex La Frombois
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `LA FROMBOIS, ALEX`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_047#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. No figure is drawn (L1).

what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.

District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.

what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.

Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. Aggregate mix follows the supplied specification; exact presence, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. H-family boarding-house massing currently uses a generic frame dwelling/block archetype.

fabric_basis.words: red-painted clapboard on a balloon frame under a new roof — a merchant's or professional house, new-built (rule F-M: a merchant's or professional man's by its type)

sizes.upper_windows: ceil(21 crowded beds / 3 to a chamber) = 7, held to 5-10 (the house's own five bays to the H3 crosswalk's top) = 7: 7 across the upper storey of the front and of the rear
sizes.stovepipes: ceil(9 ordinary beds / 3 to a stove) = 3, held to 2-6: 3
sizes.chimneys: not sized by the beds: the two brick stacks are the household's kitchen and common-room hearths, and the stoves the beds add go out through the roof as stovepipes

lodging.note: The town model puts a boarding house at 9 people on an ordinary night and 21 when full, from the 1840 household tail (p90 and p99 of 964 Chicago households). This building takes the share of its class's total that its 195 m² of enclosed floor (98 m² × 2 storeys) is of the class's floor area.
lodging.replaceable_by: Any source that states this house's rooms, beds or lodgers on a dated day: an advertisement counting its rooms, a traveller's account of how many it slept, a licence return. A stated capacity retires the apportioned one outright.

occupancy.statement: 9 on this card against an ordinary night's 9 beds: 1 seated here from elsewhere in the layer, where no source gives them a roof, 7 drawn against the order book's lodging buckets for beds that were standing empty, a keeper drawn for a roof this programme raised.
occupancy.keeper_owed: Minted by this stage as the keeper. T-1533 drew this keeper's own children here — 1 of them — out of the book's `under_10` lodging cells, at the size the 1840 histogram gives the household. What is still owed is a SPOUSE, which no rule this project has made can draw for a keeper who is a woman; the ledger's `keeper_families` row states it, and the staffing under a keeper is T-1183's.
